items.title: 53571_Mary Lou Williams oral history interview
items.q: Peggy Hitchcock, she was very good to me. She gave me her trousseau.

ctx.x: very wealthy people and if I got them I couldn't move them in the store. One girl, one of the cousins of the Mellons, was here - Peggy Hitchcock, she was very good to me. She gave me her trousseau. I couldn't move them. Some of the dresses were almost $700. I took them back to her. If everyone in Harlem knew what I had in the store when I moved up here they probably would have broken into it because I had $200 shoes, and oh, just things.
How were you able to be in the store enough to sell anything?
